newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks extend slide on auction forecast.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks extend slide on auction forecast.

text.p: Mexican stocks fell Tuesday on worries of higher-than-expected increases in primary interest rates at a weekly Treasury bill auction.

"What hit the market more than anything was the expectation of greater increases in primary interest rates, that's what it moved on today," said Hector Jimenez, a stock analyst at the Inverlat brokerage in Mexico City said.
The leading IPC share index ended down 40.68 points, or 1.06 percent, at 3,804.12. Trading volume was unremarkable at 88.4 million shares.

A Reuter survey of nine money market traders in Mexico City showed they forecast that at Tuesday's auction Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes, or Treasury bills, at an average rate of 22.09 percent, which would be up 0.93 percentage point from last week's auction.
"Nonetheless, we believe the IPC is consolidating and will seek to halt its slide at a floor of 3,750 points," Jimenez added.
Analysts said international factors were still weighing on the market.

"The market is still awaiting, and we may even say nervous, over the forthcoming (U.S.) Federal Open Market Committee meeting," said Esteban Rojas, deputy head of research at the Arka brokerage, which could indicate the future of interest rates.
"What's more, the bourse is still in a waiting period before the U.S. House of Representatives votes on certifying Mexico (as a drugs war ally)," he added.
On the broad market, 99 stocks changed hands, of which decliners outnumbered gainers by 51 to 23.
Telecomms firm Telemex L class was the most heavily traded decliner, off 10 centavos (1 cent) at 16.00 pesos ($2.01).

Financial group Abaco L shares topped the decliners' list, off 23 centavos (3 cents) at 2.11 pesos (26 cents). Traders said financial stocks in general ended down on predicted interest rate hikes that would tend to increase their bad-loans burden.
Retail stock Cifra B class was another prominent slider, ending off 93 centavos (12 cents) at 11.38 pesos ($1.43).
Glassmaker Vitro was a leading gainer, ending up 80 centavos (10 cents) at 22.00 pesos ($2.76) following news that Libbey said it would buy a $100 million stake in the firm's tableware business.
